source: NLM MeSH AI/ML branch (all descriptor IDs verified live against id.nlm.nih.gov, 2026-08-26) plus 4 clearly-flagged project extensions where MeSH has no descriptor
decision_note: Two-axis split agreed with Gavin: learning_paradigm (how the model learns; textbook-consensus axis) and model_family (what kind of system/method family; cross-cutting, multi-label). Gavin's two amendments incorporated: (1) AI agent vs agentic system as two separate terms -- different degrees of agency, task-specific agent vs Biomni-style system; (2) classical machine learning added so classic supervised/unsupervised methods (SVM, random forest, k-means, ...) have a family to land in -- individual classical methods have their own real MeSH descriptors (e.g. Support Vector Machine D060388, Random Forest D000093743) but MeSH has no family-level grouping for them, hence project extension.

learning_paradigm.guidance: How the model learns. Usually exactly 1; use 2 only for genuine hybrids.

terms.label: semi-supervised
terms.definition: Learning from a mix of labelled and unlabelled data. Standard textbook category; verified absent from MeSH (exact + contains lookups empty).

model_family.guidance: What kind of system/method family. Cross-cutting and multi-label: a supervised paper can be deep learning + ensemble at once. Boundary between the two classical terms: non-neural statistical learning methods go to 'classical machine learning'; shallow/non-deep neural approaches go to 'classic neural network'; deep architectures go to 'deep learning'.

terms.label: classical machine learning
terms.definition: Non-neural, non-deep statistical learning methods: SVM, random forest, gradient boosting, k-NN, decision trees, k-means and other classical clustering, etc. Community-consensus term (the standard 'classical ML vs deep learning' dichotomy); individual member methods have their own real MeSH descriptors (Support Vector Machine D060388, Random Forest D000093743, Cluster Analysis D016000) but MeSH has no family-level grouping.

terms.label: classic neural network
terms.definition: Shallow/non-deep neural network approaches (e.g. a plain MLP); deep architectures go to 'deep learning' instead.

terms.label: AI agent
terms.definition: A task-specific agent applying an AI model with some autonomy and/or tool use to a defined task -- a single agent, limited scope of agency. Verified absent from MeSH (every 'agent' descriptor is pharmacological).

terms.label: agentic system
terms.definition: A multi-component autonomous system orchestrating models, tools, and plans across tasks (e.g. Biomni-style systems) -- a higher degree of agency than a single task-specific AI agent. Verified absent from MeSH.
